analysis.title: Paul Donovan's daily audio: Mundanity upon mundanity
key_insights: The Fed's policy decision carried no surprises. Chair Warsh signaled a desire to reduce the number of policy meetings in 2027, which UBS says means less policy flexibility during economic and political turmoil.
UBS says the path remains open for further Fed rate increases.

Warsh previously cited, without detailing, a breadth of inflation measure. UBS says it may have been chosen because it was guaranteed to improve, and it should improve in the US consumer deflator indicator due today.
Rising gasoline prices and the pass-through of higher diesel costs to other prices will raise headline inflation. Fading tariff effects will reduce the number of prices that are rising significantly.
US Q3 GDP is seen as less significant because UBS expects it to be revised dramatically in the coming months. UBS expects the consumer to stay resilient.
AI investment should continue to support US investment, while pushing imports to be a larger drag on GDP growth.
The ECB is expected to follow the Fed in holding rates. The liveliest part of the press conference is likely to be speculation about Lagarde's departure date.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The breadth measure Warsh cited should improve as fading tariff effects reduce the number of prices rising significantly, even as headline inflation rises on gasoline and diesel pass-through.
UBS expects the figure to be revised dramatically in the coming months, so it matters less. Consumer resilience and AI investment are expected to continue, with imports a larger drag.

macro_indicators.reading: No change surprise; further rate increases remain possible
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed delivered no surprises. Warsh's wish to hold fewer meetings in 2027 reduces policy flexibility.
The ECB is expected to follow the Fed in doing nothing.

risk_factors: Fewer Fed policy meetings in 2027 would reduce policy flexibility during economic and political turmoil.
Rising gasoline prices and diesel cost pass-through could push headline inflation higher.
AI-driven import growth may become a larger drag on US GDP growth.
Q3 GDP is likely to be revised dramatically.
